title: CLR/45/2008 of UMESH CHANDRA AGARWAL Vs SMT. USHA RANI AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 45 of 2008
Umesh Chandra Agarwal. .........Revisionist.
Versus
Smt. Usha Rani & others. .........Respondents.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the revisionist / defendant.
Mr. J.C. Belwal, Advocate for respondent No. 1 / plaintiff.
BARIN GHOSH, C.J. (Oral)
 Respondent / plaintiff purchased the property from one Murlidhar,
whereas Murlidhar had purchased the property from one Laxmi Devi.
According to the respondent / plaintiff, it is Murlidhar, who made the
construction, and Murlidhar inducted the father of the revisionist /
defendant as a tenant. In the suit, the question was, whether the
construction was made by Murlidhar, or, whether, before Murlidhar had
purchased the property, there was an existing construction; inasmuch as, if
the construction had been made by Murlidhar, as was claimed by the
respondent / plaintiff, then the property will be outside the purview of the
Rent Control Act and, if not, the same will be within the Rent Control Act.
The revisionist / defendant contended in his written statement that the
premises, which was let out to his father, was constructed by Laxmi Devi
and, to substantiate the said contention, revisionist / defendant placed
reliance upon a certified copy of the assessment register of the
municipality in respect of the property in question. Accepting the
certified copy of the said assessment register, the suit was dismissed,
inasmuch as, it was held that the building / premises has been assessed
before the cut-off date mentioned in the Act and, accordingly, protections
provided to the tenant under the Rent Control Act are applicable.
2. On a Revision preferred by the respondent / plaintiff, this Court
interfered with the order of dismissal of the suit and directed re-consideration of the matter de novo and, in particular, whether the

2
provisions of the Rent Control Act apply to the building in question or
not. Subsequent thereto, no new evidence was tendered, although the
respondent / plaintiff brought on record the sale deed by which she
obtained the property in question from Murlidhar and also certified copy
of the assessment register of the municipality in respect of the building.
3. The fact remains that, whereas, in the certified copy relied by the
revisionist / defendant, the premises has been shown as 116; in the
certified copy relied by the respondent / plaintiff, the number of the
building has been shown as 116/1. Therefore, these two certificates are in
relation to two different properties. From the judgment under revision, it
does not appear that the court applied its mind as to which of these
certified registers applies to the premises being the subject matter of the
suit. The court also totally failed to take notice of the fact that the
respondent / plaintiff has not pleaded in the plaint the number of the suit
property. Having had done so, the court felt that the certified assessment
register relied by the revisionist / defendant is forged, inasmuch as, there
are alleged manipulations. The original record is before me. I have
looked into the certified copy of the assessment register, which was relied
by the revisionist / defendant and I have not been able to locate anything
or any interpolation on the basis whereof a prudent person could come to a
conclusion that the certified copy relied by the revisionist / defendant is
forged. In order to come to the conclusion that the certified copy has been
obtained from a forged assessment register, the court below relied upon
yet another certified copy of the register submitted by the respondent /
plaintiff and, on the basis thereof, came to the conclusion that the said
certified copy relied by the revisionist / defendant is copy of a forged
register. The manner, in which the court has proceeded, is unprecedented.
It was well within the competence of the court, even at the instance of the
respondent / plaintiff, to call for production of the original register.
Instead of doing that, the court purported to rely upon a purported certified
copy of the xerox copy of the alleged original register. In law, photocopy
is not even a document, which can be looked at. No person, in law, has
been authorised to certify anything by producing a photocopy of the

3
original. A xerox or a photostat copy is not even a secondary evidence in
accordance with law. No authority, under any law, can certify
authenticity of a photostat or a xerox copy of any document. In order to
establish that the certified copy furnished by the revisionist / defendant is
certified copy of a manipulated document, it was obligatory on the part of
the respondent / plaintiff to produce the original by summoning the same
before the court. The respondent / plaintiff could not rely upon a
photostat or a xerox copy said to have been certified by some officer of
the municipality.
4. In the circumstances, the Revision Application is allowed; the
judgment is set aside; and the matter is remitted back to the court. The
court below is directed to proceed de novo with the matter; take fresh
evidence; and ignore all the evidence tendered until today; but, only after
the plaint has been suitably amended and the schedule of the property,
being the subject matter of the suit, has been appropriately furnished in the
plaint.
